AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working in the cardx R package.

Human-facing contributor documentation lives in .github/CONTRIBUTING.md. This file is the condensed, directive version. Where they overlap, they should agree — if you change a convention, change both.

What this package is

cardx extends cards with extra Analysis Results Data (ARD) functions. cards owns the framework: the card class, the tidiers, the structural checks, and the example datasets. cardx owns the wrappers: each exported function runs one statistical method from another package (stats, survival, survey, car, emmeans, aod, smd, effectsize) and returns the result as an ARD.

Consequence: almost nothing here is novel code. Every function is a variation on the same skeleton. Before writing a new one, read the closest existing analogue and copy its shape. Do not invent a new structure.

Canonical exemplars, in order of increasing complexity:

File Pattern
R/ard_stats_chisq_test.R Simplest complete wrapper. The default template.
R/ard_stats_t_test.R Two exports sharing one help page via @rdname; shared .format_*() internal helper.
R/ard_car_vif.R No upstream broom tidier — pivot to ARD shape by hand.

Never edit these by hand

Path Why / what to do instead
R/import-standalone-*.R Vendored copies. Refresh with usethis::use_standalone("insightsengineering/standalone", "<name>").
NAMESPACE Generated by roxygen2. Run devtools::document().
man/*.Rd Generated by roxygen2. Edit the roxygen block in R/, then devtools::document().
tests/testthat/_snaps/*.md Generated by testthat. Run testthat::snapshot_accept() after verifying the diff with testthat::snapshot_review().

If a change appears to require editing a standalone file, stop and say so rather than editing it.

Non-negotiable conventions

Checklist for any new or modified exported function:

The ARD contract

Column set and order:

group1, group1_level, [group2, group2_level, ...],
variable, variable_level,
context, stat_name, stat_label, stat, fmt_fun, warning, error

stat, fmt_fun, warning, and error are list-columns.

  • context is the function name minus the ard_ prefix, snake case. ard_car_vif() → "car_vif".
  • The formatting column is fmt_fun. fmt_fn is deprecated; it exists only as a soft-deprecated argument in two survey methods. Do not write fmt_fn in new code.
  • Populate stat_label with human-readable labels — via a .df_*_stat_labels() dplyr::tribble() left-joined on stat_name and finished with dplyr::coalesce(stat_label, stat_name), or an inline dplyr::case_when() for a short list.

Validate the result with cards::check_ard_structure(); it must run silently.

Use the internal vocabulary — do not add dependencies

Hard Imports are exactly: cards, cli, dplyr, glue, lifecycle, rlang, tidyr. Do not add to Imports. A statistical package goes in Suggests with a minimum version and is called as pkg::fun().

Much of purrr, stringr, forcats, and tibble is already vendored and callable unqualified. Do not reach for the namespaced version, and do not add these packages as dependencies:

File Provides (call these bare)
R/import-standalone-purrr.R map(), map_chr(), map_lgl(), map2(), imap(), pmap(), keep(), discard(), compact(), reduce(), transpose()
R/import-standalone-stringr.R str_detect(), str_replace(), str_replace_all(), str_remove(), str_extract(), str_trim(), str_squish(), str_split(), str_pad(), word()
R/import-standalone-forcats.R fct_relevel(), fct_collapse(), fct_inorder(), fct_infreq(), fct_rev(), fct_expand(), fct_na_value_to_level()
R/import-standalone-tibble.R deframe(), enframe(), remove_rownames(), rownames_to_column()
R/import-standalone-checks.R check_not_missing(), check_data_frame(), check_class(), check_scalar(), check_string(), check_logical(), check_range(), check_integerish(), check_n_levels(), check_binary(), …
R/import-standalone-check_pkg_installed.R check_pkg_installed(), is_pkg_installed(), skip_if_pkg_not_installed()
R/import-standalone-cli_call_env.R set_cli_abort_call(), get_cli_abort_call()

Documentation

  • Every @param opens with a parenthesized type, then \cr, then an indented description: (`data.frame`)\cr, (scalar `numeric`)\cr, ([`tidy-select`][dplyr::dplyr_tidy_select])\cr.

  • @return for new functions is an ARD data frame of class 'card'. Older files often say just ARD data frame; use the fuller wording in new code, and do not “fix” existing ones as a drive-by.

  • @family is not used in this package. Grouping is done in _pkgdown.yml.

  • Examples needing a suggested package must be guarded, listing every suggested package the example touches:

    #' @examplesIf cardx:::is_pkg_installed("broom")
#' @examplesIf cardx:::is_pkg_installed(c("survival", "broom", "ggsurvfit"))

    Use cards::ADSL / ADTTE / ADLB / ADAE as example data. Unguarded @examples only when the example needs nothing beyond Imports.

Tests

  • tests/testthat/test-<function_name>.R, mirroring R/ one-to-one.
  • skip_if_pkg_not_installed(c("broom", ...)) on line 1, outside any test_that() — not testthat::skip_if_not_installed(). Include withr when the file uses withr::local_options().
  • tests/testthat.R runs test_check("cardx", stop_on_warning = TRUE), so any unexpected warning fails the suite.
  • Four tests are expected for a new ARD function:
    1. Correctness vs. the wrapped function, via cards::get_ard_statistics(...) compared with the raw call, ignore_attr = TRUE.
    2. Additivity — variables = c(A, B) equals dplyr::bind_rows() of the single-variable results.
    3. Failures land in the error/warning column instead of aborting.
    4. Last test in the file: test_that("fn() follows ard structure", ...) with expect_silent(... |> cards::check_ard_structure()). Pass method = FALSE if the ARD has no method statistic.
  • Snapshots: expect_snapshot(x |> as.data.frame()), and withr::local_options(list(width = 250)) at the top for wide ARDs.
  • Target 100% coverage on new code.

Easily forgotten steps

These are the four things most often missed. Check all of them before reporting done:

  1. _pkgdown.yml — add the new topic under the matching subtitle: "{pkg} package". The pkgdown build fails on a documented topic missing from the reference index.
  2. devtools::document(), then commit man/ and NAMESPACE. CI runs roxygen with auto-update: false and fails on stale generated docs.
  3. inst/WORDLIST — add any new jargon; the CI spelling job checks against it.
  4. NEWS.md — a bullet under # cardx (development version): complete sentence, past tense, backticked function names with trailing (), issue/PR number in parentheses at the end, e.g. (#310, @handle).

Verification

styler::style_pkg()
devtools::document()
devtools::test()
spelling::spell_check_package()
devtools::check()

devtools::check() is the real gate — it runs examples, so a missing or wrong @examplesIf guard surfaces there and nowhere else. Do not report a change as verified on the strength of devtools::test() alone.

What CI enforces

Job Fails when
roxygen (auto-update: false) man/ or NAMESPACE is stale relative to the roxygen comments
style (auto-update: false) styler::style_pkg() would change a file
R-CMD-check Standard check on macOS/Windows/Ubuntu across R devel, release, oldrel-1
R-CMD-check-oldrel Check on oldrel-2/-3 with only hard dependencies installed — this is what the check_pkg_installed() / @examplesIf / skip_if_pkg_not_installed() guards exist for
spelling A word is absent from inst/WORDLIST
coverage Coverage regresses
docs (pkgdown) A documented topic is missing from _pkgdown.yml

Git

  • Branch from main as <issue_id>_<short_description>, e.g. 420_fix_vif_backticks.
  • Never commit directly to main.
  • Merge via “Squash and merge” or “Rebase and merge”.
  • Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.
